items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-10-07
items.q: I was working out there last with Mealy the Harmonade

ctx.x: And very seldom we, everybody like the way we wipe down. They just like to get work holes quite nice, just want white bands in there, well that's all the children do.
But Lawrence, I mean, uh, Gentile and, not Gentile, I was working out there last with Mealy the Harmonade, you and that man got so they couldn't get along. That's where he was. That Moss. Moss.
Also, they put a white hillbilly band in there.

items.title: Billie Pierce and De De Pierce Interview, 1959-04-02
items.q: Now this other band here, I'm wondering when that was with D.D. and Emile Barnes, who's the guitar player?

ctx.x: Yeah, I'm looking through them, I'm sure. I'll put this in with that. Yeah, that's why I keep them all in together, you know.
Now this other band here, I'm wondering when that was with D.D. and Emile Barnes, who's the guitar player? I don't know. That's Emile, what's the name of D.D.?
Raleigh? Yeah, Emile Raleigh. Oh, yeah.

items.title: Billie Pierce, De De Pierce, Israel Gorman, Joseph "Kid Twat" Butler Interview, 1963-11-20
items.q: You've made some records with different people, too. Emile Barnes.

ctx.x: Well, Paul and I, Paul Barnes and I, we got a band, Sunset Syncopator, and we've done a lot of work here, too. There's a lot of different, you know, outfits.
You've made some records with different people, too. Emile Barnes. Yeah, I mean, when we were born, yeah.
Oh, yeah. We just lived together. Bill Rossman. Yeah, we're watching.
